errors.accessTokenTypeRejected: MongoDB rejected your identity provider's access token type. Turn on “Use ID token instead of access token” for this connection.
errors.browserLaunchFailed: MQLens could not open your system browser. Set a default browser, then try again.
errors.consentDenied: The login was denied. Approve the request in your browser to continue.
errors.discoveryFailed: MQLens could not read your identity provider's configuration. Check network access to the provider.
errors.hostNotAllowed: This MongoDB host is not in the allowed hosts for OIDC. Add it under Allowed hosts if you trust this deployment.
errors.idpOauthError: Your identity provider rejected the login request. Check the application registration for this deployment.
errors.insecureEndpoint: The identity provider endpoint is not HTTPS. MQLens will not send a login over an unencrypted connection.
errors.loginOkPingFailed: Login succeeded, but the database did not respond. Check the host, TLS and network settings.
errors.missingClientId: This deployment did not supply an OIDC client id, so a browser login cannot start. Ask your administrator to configure one.
errors.portUnavailable: MQLens could not open port 27097 to receive the login. Another login may be using it, in MQLens, mongosh or Compass. Finish or cancel that login, then try again.
errors.stateMismatch: The login response did not match this request and was rejected. Start the login again.
errors.timedOut: The browser login expired. Start the login again.
errors.tokenExchangeFailed: MQLens could not exchange the login for a token. If your network uses a proxy, note that the identity provider is reached directly, not through the connection's SOCKS5 proxy.
errors.tokenRejected: MongoDB rejected the login token. Confirm your account has access to this deployment.

auth.oidcAllowedHostsHelp: Only needed for self-managed deployments. MongoDB Atlas hosts are already allowed. Comma-separated, e.g. mongo.corp.example.com
auth.oidcNote: Login opens in your system browser. Your credentials are entered only at your identity provider — MQLens never sees them, and no token is saved.
auth.oidcUseIdToken: Use ID token instead of access token
auth.oidcUseIdTokenHelp: Turn this on if MongoDB rejects your identity provider's access tokens (for example cidaas). MongoDB then checks the ID token, whose audience is your client ID.
auth.x509Note: Requires TLS with a client certificate (TLS tab).
